title: Set operations are concatenation, `unique` and semi/anti joins
description: Polars has no set-operation node: `pl.concat` is `UNION ALL`, and `unique` after it is `UNION`. `INTERSECT` and `EXCEPT` are a semi and an anti join on every column with `nulls_equal=True`, then `unique`: without `nulls_equal` NULL rows never match (a semi join drops them, an anti join keeps them).
`INTERSECT ALL` and `EXCEPT ALL` have no direct form; the reference's numbering of equal rows (a `cum_count` over every column) would write them.
reference: `UNION ALL` is bag union and `UNION DISTINCT` its `distinct`; `INTERSECT` and `EXCEPT` are semi and anti joins with NULLs equal, then `DISTINCT`, and the `ALL` forms number equal rows (#344).

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.
